idempotency_key.description: Optional client-supplied key. A request repeated with the same key is never executed again: the service returns the original outcome. Reuse the key when retrying the same request.

args.summary: The v2.3.1 deployment of checkout-api caused failing health checks across all regions. Rolled back to v2.3.0, the most recent healthy production release. The first rollback attempt partially failed (us-east succeeded; us-west and eu-west remained on v2.3.1), so the rollback was retried and completed successfully. All regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) are now on v2.3.0, healthy, with error rate reduced from 18% to 0.2%.
args.title: checkout-api rollback to v2.3.0 after v2.3.1 health check failures

trace.error_message: Request to create_incident timed out after 30000ms

trace.final:
All done. Here's a summary of what happened:

1. **Checked deployment history**: v2.3.0 was the most recent healthy production release (v2.3.1, the latest deploy, was unhealthy).
2. **Rolled back checkout-api to v2.3.0**: The first attempt partially failed — us-east rolled back successfully but us-west and eu-west remained on v2.3.1 with an 18% error rate. I retried the rollback, which completed successfully in all regions.
3. **Verified recovery**: All regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) are now running v2.3.0, the service is healthy, and the error rate dropped to 0.2%.
4. **Opened a SEV2 incident** (INC-0001) describing the health check failures, the rollback, the partial failure and retry, and the recovery. The incident creation call initially timed out, but a check of the incident list confirmed it was created successfully, so no retry was needed — avoiding a duplicate incident.

transcript.content: The incident creation timed out. Let me check whether it actually got created before retrying:
transcript.reasoning_content: Timeout — need to retry. No idempotency key was used the first time; on retry I should supply an idempotency key to avoid duplicate incidents in case the first one actually got created. Actually the first request had no key, so retrying with a key could still duplicate if the first one went through. Best practice: retry with idempotency key. But first, let me check list_incidents to see if the original was created.
